title: Documentation MCP for consistent authoring and publishing
objective: Design and implement a documentation MCP module that helps agents discover, author, validate, maintain, and publish project documentation consistently across repository docs, GitHub Pages, and other configured documentation destinations.

acceptance_criteria.text: A documented information architecture defines canonical documentation sources, document types, ownership, audience, lifecycle/status, metadata, and the relationship between docs, decisions, and tickets.

The MCP exposes tools to discover/search/read documentation and to create, update, and deprecate/archive docs through validated, auditable engine-only writes constrained to configured documentation roots.

Document templates and validation enforce project conventions, required metadata/structure, link integrity, and cross-document consistency without duplicating ticket-specific test procedures or decision history.

The module can build a deterministic, previewable publication output from canonical sources, with configurable navigation, relative-link handling, asset handling, and exclusion of private/internal material.

A documented adapter boundary supports at least one code-documentation target (for example GitHub Pages) and one portable/wiki-oriented Markdown export, without coupling canonical content to a single hosting vendor.

Publishing is explicit and safe: preview/dry-run is available, credentials are not stored in documentation or build artifacts, and a failed publish preserves source docs and reports actionable diagnostics.

Automated tests cover engine-only writes and audit/lock behavior, path traversal and duplicate handling, metadata/templates, broken links, deterministic build output, private-doc exclusion, and publication adapter failures.

needed: Choose and document the documentation source/inventory and metadata schema, including canonical-source rules and how decisions/tickets are referenced.
Specify MCP tool contracts and engine-only write/audit/lock/index guarantees; identify whether this extends little-mester MCP or is a separately versioned module.
Select an initial code-doc publication adapter and a portable/wiki Markdown export target; document preview, credentials, and failure behavior.
Prototype CI validation and deterministic generated-site/export checks on representative existing project docs.
Define migration/ownership policy for existing README, docs, decisions, runbooks, and generated reference material without creating duplicate sources of truth.
